title: Paoletti at Warren Easton and a Mayer-system flute from Fazola
summary: Paoletti headed music at Warren Easton and led a municipal Hussar band shown in a photo; talk of Mayer-system flutes obtained from Fazola.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did they have any teachers in high school? Any music teachers that you remember?
I think Palletti was at Warren Easton. He was the head of the music there.
Is that the same guy who used to be out at Spanish Fort?
We have a picture of his concert band.
Well he was a teacher when I went to Warren Easton.
Let me get that picture for you. What were you saying? That's the same fella huh? Uh huh. It's a picture of Palletti's municipal Hussar band. Hussar band. A German band isn't it?
It was supposed to be I guess.
The Hussars were German weren't they? I don't know.
He beats me. I forget. I'll have to look that up. We got a dictionary guarantee. Tell us.
I had a flute like that. The wooden Maya system.
That's right. The BAME came in on the flute. He replaced Maya.
Yeah. I had a Maya system flute which I got from Fazola. He got from I don't know where and he bought a BAME system silver flute and then I got one and I traded the flute into Whirlands.
So Palletti was there at the school and-
